newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Mark ends down on EMU worries, bourses fall.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Mark ends down on EMU worries, bourses fall.

text.p: The mark weakened against the dollar and sterling on Monday as anxiety resurfaced over the European single currency, and European bourses ended down sharply, hit by a poor performance on Wall Street.

London stocks finished well down as strong economic data also revived fears of higher interest rates. Paris floor trade and Frankfurt computer dealings ended a lacklustre day with losses of over one percent.

But currency markets saw most of the day's excitement. Nerves over the future of European economic and monetary union (EMU) drove the dollar up by a pfennig to 1.7465 marks, a 40-month peak, before it fell back slightly in late trading.
Sterling also rose to a five-year high against the German currency.
Traders moved in on safe haven currencies after a rift within Germany's ruling alliance over EMU widened at the weekend with one of its partners raising the prospect of leaving the coalition.
"We are continuing to see this structural desire to shift out of core EMU currencies into alternatives," said Shean Shepley, international economist at CS First Boston.

The German dispute pits members of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) against its Bavarian sister party, the Christian Social Union (CSU), and above all Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber.

Stoiber is calling for a delay in monetary union if the entry criteria are weakened. He has threatened to block German membership of EMU in the upper house of parliament unless the criteria are strictly met.
But Kohl defended his stance against Stoiber, saying on Monday his government was fully united in its drive to launch the euro currency on time in 1999.
"Europe has big problems to get over and the way the politicians are going about it is not very constructive," Shepley added.

The dollar's rally was not seen petering out. "The dollar is trending higher and there is clear evidence that people are eager to buy on dips. I think we could see a dollar/mark rate of 1.85 by year-end," said currency strategist Brian Martin at Barclays de Zeote Wedd.

A higher-than-expected reading in the Chicago Purchasing Managers Index for June and a rise in U.S. single-family home sales in May confirmed the U.S. economy was gearing up for further growth and possibly higher interest rates, which also helped lift the dollar.

With the German currency already vulnerable over EMU, sterling was given a boost, reaching 2.8991 marks near the close, when strong data on British consumer credit fuelled chances of an interest rate increase.

In equity markets, London opened higher but turned negative as sentiment was knocked by the fears of interest rate rises and nervousness ahead of the Labour government's first Budget on Wednesday. The mood was aggvravated by Wall Street early losses.

"This is just the start of what could be a very volatile week," commented one trader. "Nobody is interested in taking things on before the Budget...everyone is just getting out of the way," said another.

The FTSE 100 index closed 35.7 points lower at 4,604.6, shedding a 20 points made in early trade after the buoyant consumer credit figures reinforced the need for measures in the budget to dampen spending.
"The figures confirmed the strength in the consumer sector and the need for something to slow it down," said Stuart Weatherby, economist at Panmure Gordon.
European markets are likely remain edgy this week ahead of a meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve's monetary policy-makers.

Few analysts expect an immediate American interest rate rise but the U.S. central bank is likely to be alert for any signs that the underlying strength of the economy could feed inflation in coming months.
Frankfurt initially made modest gains before floor trade lost confidence and the blue-chip DAX index ended down 9.64 points at 3785.77.
Computer trading on the IBIS index fell more sharply, registering losses of 1.13 percent at the close , perhaps depressed by Wall Street's fall of over 0.5 percent as Europe ended trading..

Paris closed with losses of 1.13 percent as the weaker Wall Street unsettled investors. Car-maker Renault ended the day with losses of 4.4 percent at 148.7 francs after the closure of the Vilvoorde plant in Belgium was confirmed over the weekend.
In bullion markets, gold closed at $334.35, up slightly on the morning fix of $334.05 an ounce, its lowest for 4-1/2 years, under pressure from the strong dollar.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was at 114.53 yen and 1.7444 marks, compared with 114.62 and 1.7365 in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index finished down 35.7 points at 4,604.6.
PARIS - The CAC-40 finished down 32.78 to 2,858.26 points.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed down 9.64 points at 3,785.77.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $334.35 an ounce against $337.15 at Friday's close. Silver was at $4.69, down five cents in late trade.
